Subject: Aurora security questionnaire — data geography & retention (hosted API)

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this — Aurora's security team has a short set of questions about how Redwood handles customer data for the hosted API. We're consolidating answers for our procurement and security review. Can you confirm the following (short answers are fine, we may ask for evidence later):

1) Where is customer request/response data stored by default (region / cloud provider)?
2) Does Redwood persist any request content or generated responses beyond request latency? If yes, what is the default retention period and what data is retained?
3) Are there options to disable retention for our account or to configure a residency (e.g., store data only in us-east-1)?
4) Deletion: if Aurora requests a full erase of conversation data for a given project, what is the end-to-end timeline and what systems are affected (index, backups, logs)?
5) Backups & snapshots: frequency and retention window; are backups geo-replicated?
6) Audit & logs: how long are audit trails (api keys, token usage, admin access) kept? Can we request an extract prior to deletion?
7) Encryption & key management: is data encrypted at rest and in transit; do you support customer-managed keys (CMK / KMS)?
8) Any evidence you can attach (retention matrix, dataflow diagram, SOC 2 scope) would be helpful.

I've attached our questionnaire to this thread. If you prefer, a short call works — our security lead is available Thursday afternoon PT.

Best,
Elena

Aurora Financial

Sooj, Karthik — forwarding Aurora's questions. Drafted quick answers below; can you scan for accuracy and push back on any retention timelines that are too optimistic? We should keep the public-hosted defaults conservative but call out enterprise options.

--- DRAFT ANSWERS (short form) ---
1) Default storage location: Redwood's hosted API processes requests in the region tied to the customer's account. For Aurora's primary provisioned region we would serve from AWS us-east-1 by default.

2) Persistence: By default, Redwood retains request and response payloads for 30 days for billing, abuse detection, and troubleshooting. Retained fields include full request/response text, associated metadata (request id, model, token counts), and delivery logs.

3) Residency options: We support region scoping for accounts (US, EU, APAC) on hosted plans; for strict residency and no-persistence requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. Some enterprise customers can opt for a 'no-retention' hosted setting (data not stored beyond ephemeral processing) on a contractual basis.

4) Deletion workflow: Customer-initiated erasure triggers a staged purge: (a) mark for deletion immediately, (b) remove primary records within 7 days, (c) purge backups/snapshots within 90 days. Audit logs of the deletion action are retained for 180 days for compliance traceability.

5) Backups: Snapshot cadence varies by storage layer; primary DB snapshots retained for 90 days and are geo-replicated as part of our provider managed service.

6) Audit & logs: Operational logs (request-level) default 30 days; security audit logs and admin access records retained 12 months. We can provide an extract on request prior to deletion.

7) Encryption: TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest by default. We support customer-managed KMS keys for enterprise accounts.

8) Evidence: attaching a short retention matrix and a simplified dataflow diagram; SOC 2 report available under NDA.

Notes for Soojin: pls edit phrasing around "remove primary records within 7 days" if we need a longer window. Also we should decide whether to promise an immediate scrub of inference KV caches or call out "best-effort".

Thanks — Monica

Elena,

Thanks for the clear list — please find our consolidated responses below and two attachments (retention matrix + high‑level dataflow diagram). Happy to hop on the call Thursday if you want to run through details.

Short answers (hosted API)
1) Default region: Requests are served from the region associated with your Redwood account. By default we provision Aurora's hosted tenancy in AWS us-east-1 (Virginia) unless you request another available region.

2) Persistence: By default Redwood retains request and response payloads (customer-provided prompts and model outputs) for 30 days. Retention applies to full request/response text, request metadata (request id, model name, token counts), and delivery/tracing logs. We keep this short window to enable billing reconciliation, abuse detection, and troubleshooting.

3) Residency & opt-out: We offer region scoping on hosted plans (US, EU, APAC). For customers requiring zero-retention we offer a contractual hosted configuration for enterprise accounts that disables long‑term storage (requests processed ephemerally). For workloads with strict regulatory residency, we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments where data residency and retention policies are fully controlled by the customer.

4) Deletion: On a customer-initiated erasure we perform a staged purge: mark identifiers immediately, remove primary records and user-visible artifacts within 7 days, and sweep provider-managed backups/snapshots within 90 days (final timing depends on underlying provider retention semantics). Operational audit records that document the deletion action are retained for 180 days to satisfy audit requirements; copies of audit logs can be exported on request prior to data purge.

5) Backups & replication: Database snapshots are taken at regular intervals and are geo-replicated by our cloud provider as part of their managed service. Snapshot retention is 90 days by default for hosted accounts.

6) Audit & logs: Request-level operational logs are retained 30 days. Security and admin audit logs (API key creation, admin console access, role changes) are retained 12 months. We can provide a CSV export of relevant logs prior to deletion on a case-by-case basis.

7) Encryption & KMS: All data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256). Customer-managed KMS keys are supported for enterprise accounts (we provide integration guidance and an onboarding checklist).

8) Evidence: Attached: "redwood-hosted-retention-summary.pdf" (one-page retention matrix) and "dataflow-diagram.png" (simplified flow showing ephemeral processing and persistent stores). Our SOC 2 report is available under NDA; we can route that through your security intake process.

If you'd like wording for your procurement questionnaire (short bullet answers), we can produce that as a one-page Q&A. Also happy to schedule a short review call (Thu afternoon PT works for us).
